$comment: Packages whose pinned release exists ONLY to clear a security advisory.
These are the overrides that must never be expressed as a lockfile-only
edit. pnpm resolves every version from the manifest, so a pnpm-lock.yaml
that pins brace-expansion@1.1.21 with nothing in pnpm-workspace.yaml to
back it up is undone by the first plain `pnpm install` — the tree silently
returns to the vulnerable release and `pnpm audit` goes red again. That is
exactly what happened in 8be206f; `scripts/check-security-pins.mjs` exists so
the next one is blocked at CI instead of discovered by a Trivy scan.
Per pin, the checker enforces three invariants:
1. every key in `overrides` is present in pnpm-workspace.yaml with exactly
the declared value (the durable pin);
2. every key is recorded in the pnpm-lock.yaml `overrides` block with the
same value (proof the lockfile was generated WITH the override);
3. what the lockfile actually resolved agrees with the override:
`resolved`     - exact set of versions allowed in the tree. Use when
the override value is an exact version; any other
version of the package in the tree is a violation.
`minResolved`  - floor for every resolved version. Use when the
override value is a range (`>=x.y.z`), so a newer
patched release does not need a manifest edit.
Adding a pin is deliberate, not automatic: a fourth advisory family means
editing this file in the same PR that adds the override. Removing a pin is
legitimate once an upstream release makes the override unnecessary.
Range-qualified keys (`brace-expansion@<2`) are pnpm override syntax, not
semver ranges to evaluate here — they are compared as literal strings.

pins.name: brace-expansion
pins.why: Quadratic-time CPU DoS on `{a},b}` rewrites, plus uncontrolled recursion. minimatch@3.x pulls the 1.x line, minimatch@10.x the 5.x line; both were flagged HIGH by pnpm audit and by Trivy.

pins.name: fast-uri
pins.why: SSRF and host confusion (unvalidated port, unbalanced URI brackets), URI scheme and path normalization issues, and mailto header injection. fast-uri@3 serves ajv, fast-uri@4 serves fast-json-stringify/@fastify/ajv-compiler, so both majors need pinning.

pins.name: nanoid
pins.why: Denial of service via an infinite loop on crafted input.

pins.name: uuid
pins.why: Missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when a caller-provided buffer is used. Pinned EXACTLY to 11.1.1: a '>=11.1.1' range resolves to an ESM-only major and breaks require() in the CommonJS gaxios -> firebase-admin chain. uuid@12 dropped the CJS build.

pins.name: js-yaml
pins.why: CPU exhaustion via empty merge sources in YAML. Affects @commitlint, eslint and ~29 other transitive paths, so this is a floor rather than an exact pin.

pins.name: tar
pins.why: tar < 7.5.21. The primary fix is the pnpm version bump plus an apt/sed patch in the Dockerfile; this npm-layer override is the backstop.

pins.name: @grpc/grpc-js
pins.why: getAuthContext can return unauthorized certificates as though they were authorized, in 1.14.0-1.14.4. Pulled in via firebase-admin -> @google-cloud/firestore -> google-gax.

pins.name: @fastify/busboy
pins.why: Denial of Service in @fastify/busboy 3.2.0 and earlier; fixed in 3.2.1. A floor rather than an exact pin so a newer patched release needs no manifest edit.

pins.name: source-map-js
pins.why: Denial of Service via malformed indexed source maps in source-map-js < 1.2.2. Pulled in transitively by magicast and postcss.

pins.name: vite
pins.why: Command injection via improper file path validation in launch-editor, bundled in the vite dev server, in 8.2.0 through 8.2.3. Reached only through vitest (a devDependency), but pnpm audit and the Docker Trivy scan fail HIGH on it. Pinned EXACTLY to 8.2.4 and scoped to the 8.2 line vitest already resolves, so a newer major is not pulled in by accident.

pins.name: zod
pins.why: Memory exhaustion while validating oversized constrained collections in zod < 4.6.6 (high; pnpm audit and the Docker Trivy scan both fail on it). zod validates every gateway request and response and is used inside better-auth. A floor rather than an exact pin so a newer patched release needs no manifest edit. The frontend repo pins zod as well and must stay on the same release line, because the contract parity check builds both sides with one zod.

pins.name: better-auth
pins.why: Authentication advisories affect Better Auth releases before 1.7.7. Keep the gateway and Firestore adapter on a patched release.

pins.name: fastify
pins.why: Fastify 5.12.2 through 5.12.5 have HTTP/2 trailer denial-of-service or header validation issues. The workspace depends on Fastify 5 and can use the patched 5.12.6 floor.

pins.name: @vitest/mocker
pins.why: Optional Vitest mocker dependency in the production dependency graph is below the patched 4.1.12 release. Keep the resolved package at the patched floor.
